slides.title: Drone work in ATAK
slides.html: OpenDefence UAVOps is OpenDefence's drone operations plugin, behind the Drones button. It takes a soldier's request for a drone to the team that flies it, and brings the result back. Missions shows which drones fly now and how far each target is from you.

slides.title: From ask to result
slides.html: A forward observer asks for a strike or a recon on an enemy mark or a drawn area. The headquarters (HQ) or a platoon's tactical operations centre (TOC) hands the request to a drone team, or it goes straight to the teams the observer asked. The team plans, flies and reports the mission. The asker follows each step in OpenDefence Main's Inbox under Sent, here Hit.

slides.title: It does not fly the drone
slides.html: OpenDefence UAVOps does not fly drones. The drone shows on the map from the position it already sends, its track, here KOIRA11, or as a marker the team moves By hand. The drone team records the take-off, the landing and the result.

slides.title: Before you start
slides.html: OpenDefence UAVOps works with OpenDefence Main and needs the Data Sync plugin, whose drone feeds carry the missions from phone to phone. It opens from Drones on OpenDefence Main's thumb bar, the buttons at the bottom left of the map. Concepts explains the words used here, Starting as a user sets your role and unit, and then each role has its own chapter.
